struck: Only 21 sold in three years, at about $930,000 at the middle, about 1.6 times a house west of the bypass.
use: 21 of them sold in the three years to September 2026, at about $930,000 at the middle, about 1.7 times the middle house west of the bypass.

struck: About 220 houses back onto the inlet's marsh, all on the Georgetown side of US 17 Business.
use: About 220 houses outside Garden City sit within 30 m of the inlet's salt marsh, almost all on the creek side of US 17 Business.

struck: Horry-side villas and townhouses sold for about $320,000 (78 sales).
use: Horry-side townhouses sold for about $320,000 (70 sales).

struck: 465 homes with a Murrells Inlet city were for sale in the CRM: 202 houses, 129 condos, 33 townhouses, 58 manufactured homes and 38 lots.
use: 465 listings with a Murrells Inlet city were for sale: 202 houses, 129 condos, 33 townhouses, 58 manufactured homes, 5 multi-family buildings and 38 lots.

struck: The largest neighborhoods on the Horry side are Indigo Creek (about 560 houses), Seasons at Prince Creek (about 440, a 55+ community), The Pines of St. James (about 370), Longwood Bluffs and Wynbrooke.
use: The largest house neighborhoods on the Horry side are Indigo Creek (about 560 houses), Seasons at Prince Creek West (about 440, a 55+ community), The Pines of St. James (about 370) and Longwood Bluffs (about 260).

struck: Palm Bay and Highwood at Prince Creek are in Georgetown County, Seasons at Prince Creek is in Horry.
use: Prince Creek crosses the county line: Palm Bay is in Georgetown County, Seasons at Prince Creek West is in Horry, and Highwood is split between them.

struck: The old streets along the creek are Sunnyside, Vaux Hall, the Hermitage and Wilcox and Briggs.
use: The county's named areas on the creek side include Sunnyside, the Hermitage and Vaux Hall.

struck: On the Georgetown side, the county's own estimate uses 128.9 mills for a legal residence and 252.0 mills for a second home, plus a $96 household fee.
use: On the Georgetown side, Georgetown County's current tax estimate for district 41 uses 128.9 mills for a legal residence and 252.0 mills for other homes, plus $96 in storm water and household fees.

pattern: flood insurance is cheap|\bcheap\b[^.]{0,40}flood|high-risk zone paid about \$1,080
struck: Flood insurance is cheap for most Murrells Inlet houses. A house in a high-risk zone paid about $1,080 at the middle.
use: The middle flood insurance policy on a house cost about $590 a year on the Georgetown side and about $580 on the Horry side; in an A zone it was about $1,080, in a V zone about $2,160.

struck: Every Horry-side home is zoned for St. James Elementary, St. James Intermediate, St. James Middle and St. James High.
use: Horry-side homes are zoned for St. James schools: all but 2 of 8,945 for St. James Elementary, and all for St. James Intermediate, Middle and High.

struck: Every Georgetown-side home is zoned for the Waccamaw schools of the Georgetown County School District.
use: Georgetown-side homes are zoned for the Waccamaw schools of the Georgetown County School District.

struck: Nightly renting pays most for big houses.
use: The gap between a typical Airbnb's gross revenue and HUD's fair rent grows with size.

struck: Crazy Sister Marina and a public boat landing sit at its middle.
use: Crazy Sister Marina and the county's Murrells Inlet boat landing are at the MarshWalk's south end.

struck: Pawleys Island about 15 to 20, Market Common about 20.
use: Pawleys Island about 15, Market Common about 20.

struck: On creeks of 20 to 50 feet the dock's deck area is capped at 120 square feet, 51 to 150 feet at 160, wider at 600.
use: As a rule, on creeks of 20 to 50 feet the dock's pierhead and float area is held to 120 square feet, 51 to 150 feet to 160, wider to 600; the state can allow more in special circumstances.

struck: NOAA's station at Captain Alex's Marina on Parsonage Creek.
use: NOAA's prediction station at Captain Alex's Marina in the inlet.

struck: There are four county boat landings in the Murrells Inlet ZIP.
use: Georgetown County's boat-landing map lists four landings in the Murrells Inlet ZIP.

pattern: closed[^.]{0,40}for bacteria|anyone with a South Carolina saltwater
struck: They are open to anyone with a South Carolina saltwater fishing license. Parts of each are closed by the state for bacteria.
use: Parts of each ground are closed by SCDES, and the limit applies on no more than two days in any seven.

struck: In Garden City it is about 4 in 10 homes and 1 in 3 bills.
use: About 85 in 100 houses outside Garden City are taxed as their owner's legal residence, against about 6 in 10 Garden City houses.

struck: In its January 2025 report to the state, the county estimated the work at about $30 million and gave a preliminary finish of March 2028.
use: Georgetown County plans to dredge the inlet's creeks; in January 2025 it estimated the cost at about $30 million.

struck: Of the 55 houses for sale with no HOA, 21 are on the Georgetown side (6 on the creek side) and 23 in Garden City.
use: Of the 55 houses for sale with no HOA, 21 are on the Georgetown side (6 on the creek side), 29 are in Garden City, and 5 are on the Horry side west of the bypass.

pattern: both sides share the Murrells Inlet
struck: Both sides share the Murrells Inlet - Garden City Fire District.
use: Most of the Horry side and the Georgetown side are in the Murrells Inlet - Garden City Fire District.

struck: Groceries on the Horry side cluster near SC 707 (Publix, Lowes Foods, a Walmart Neighborhood Market); on the Georgetown side a Food Lion sits on Business 17 near the hospital.
use: On the Horry side, Publix and Lowes Foods are on SC 707 and a Walmart Neighborhood Market is on the US 17 bypass; on the Georgetown side, a Food Lion is on the US 17 bypass near the hospital.

struck: Murrells Inlet has no beach of its own on the mainland.
use: The Census's Murrells Inlet and the creek side have no ocean beach; the nearest are Huntington Beach State Park, about 9 minutes from the MarshWalk, and Garden City Beach, about 9 minutes.
